sentences.text: Customer impact lasted 3 hours 19 minutes, from 17:51 to 21:10 UTC.
We detected it at 17:52, 54 minutes before Google's first public update.
Google's report gives a 3-hour duration, but some Google products took until 01:27 UTC.
A holding statement went out at 17:56.
We run in a single Google Cloud region, so we couldn't fail over.
Staff login runs on Cloudflare Access, which failed at the same time.
Approve budget for a second region for login and API.
Impact ran 17:51–21:10 UTC, with login and API failing on Firestore and Firebase Auth 503s.
Google's Service Control quota-policy feature had no error handling or feature flag, and a policy with blank fields crash-looped it globally.
Our alert fired at 17:52; Google's status page confirmed at 18:46.
Google recovered every location except us-central1 first; our region came back last and we reached baseline at 21:10.
The GCP console was down for us.
We escalated by phone and through the account team.
Move external monitoring off Google Cloud.
Add randomised backoff to client retries.
Decide on a second region for login and API.
Between 17:51 and 21:10 UTC on 12 June, some customers couldn't log in or use our API.
Our cloud provider, Google Cloud, had a global outage in its API management system.
A new quota-policy feature had no error handling and no feature flag, and a policy change with blank fields crashed it worldwide.
Our region, us-central1, was the last to recover.
Our monitoring alerted at 17:52, 54 minutes before Google's first public update at 18:46.
We updated customers every 30 minutes and reprocessed requests that failed.
Our staff kept working through break-glass access.
Google's report says some customers' monitoring on Google Cloud failed with it, leaving them without a signal.
We're moving our external monitoring off Google Cloud.
We're adding randomised backoff to client retries.
We're assessing a second region for login and API.
